text.title: Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) Core Rules
text.summary: 11 testable rules every Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: ONE framework per service; mixed routers across files are FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal Go reviews. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handlers MUST be methods on a struct holding dependencies (services, loggers), never package-level funcs with globals.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Hexagonal architecture. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Request DTOs MUST carry binding/validate tags; controller binds + validates before calling service.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: go-playground/validator docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Responses MUST be typed structs (never `map[string]any` from a handler).
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal reviews. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Errors MUST be returned to middleware (`c.Error(err)`) that renders RFC 7807; handlers never write JSON for errors.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: error-handling methodology. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Tests MUST be table-driven over `httptest` with the actual router; mock the service interface.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Effective Go testing. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handlers MUST pass `r.Context()` / `c.Request.Context()` to service calls; never `context.Background()`. `context.Background()` belongs to `main()` and test setup only.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go context docs. `Background()` detaches from the request, so cancellation never propagates and a long downstream call keeps burning resources after the client has gone. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Use `gin.New()` / `echo.New()` and register every middleware explicitly. `gin.Default()` is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: `gin.Default()` bundles its own Logger + Recovery with opinionated formats; teams then add their own and end up running two Recoverys and logging in a format that carries no trace id. Explicit composition is the only way the order in 01-router-setup.xml is auditable. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Do NOT spawn a goroutine inside a handler that captures `c` or uses `c.Request.Context()` after the handler returns. For genuine background work derive `context.WithoutCancel(c.Request.Context())` plus an explicit timeout, and pass extracted values by argument.
rule.rationale: The request context is cancelled the moment the handler returns, so the background goroutine dies with `context canceled`; and `gin.Context` itself is request-scoped and not thread-safe, so the race detector flags it. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: A handler does exactly four things: bind request → validate via binding tags → call ONE service method → translate to HTTP. No business logic, and under 40 lines.
rule.rationale: A thin handler is testable as a transport adapter; logic inside one can only be exercised by standing up the whole HTTP stack. The 40-line bound is what makes the rule greppable rather than aspirational. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `http.Server` MUST set all four timeouts explicitly — `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`. Never leave the zero defaults. Reasonable starting values: 5s / 30s / 30s / 120s.
rule.rationale: Zero means unbounded: a client that never finishes sending headers holds a goroutine and a file descriptor forever (Slowloris), and `r.Run(":8080")` configures none of them. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold and no duplicate exists.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.

rule.statement: Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when a duplicate is found.
